issues.failure_explanation: The remark claims that for C^0 piecewise polynomials the global H^{1+theta}(Omega) norm (theta<1/2) is bounded, uniformly in h, by the sum of element-local H^{1+theta}(T) norms. The global Sobolev-Slobodeckij seminorm of the discontinuous gradient contains cross-element interaction terms that the local sum lacks. A zigzag P1 function has vanishing local gradient seminorms, but its global seminorm of the gradient is about h^{-theta} times ||grad phi||_{L^2}, so the inequality cannot hold uniformly in h. The remark also says each local term is controlled by the local H^2(T) part of |||.|||_h. This ignores that the normal-derivative jump terms in a_h are exactly what controls the cross-element part. The conclusion that (ass_stat_stab) holds for the C^0-IP method is therefore not supported by the argument given.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the localized bound by the standard discrete Sobolev-type inequality that includes the edge jump terms (sum over edges of h_e^{-1}||[d_n phi_h]||^2_{L^2(e)}, which are part of |||.|||_h for large eta). Alternatively, cite the known IP-norm result for theta<1/2, or simply keep (ass_stat_stab) as an explicit assumption for the C^0-IP case.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the hypothesis of the low-regularity stability theorem is satisfied by the C^0 interior penalty discretization is unsupported. The theorem is conditional on that hypothesis, is only included 'for completeness', and is not used for the main error estimate or the convergence theorem, so no main result is affected.
issues.title: Unsupported (false as stated) localized H^{1+theta} norm bound used to justify the stationary stability hypothesis for C^0 interior penalty elements
issues.why_classification: The defect is confined to a side remark about a non-essential stability result. Adding the jump terms, or declaring the condition an assumption, repairs it without changing any main theorem, rate, or scope.
